finding.ata_errors.action: Check SATA cables and connections. Cross-reference with SMART data to identify the affected drive.
finding.ata_errors.description: Kernel logs show repeated ATA/SATA errors. This indicates a hardware issue — typically a failing SATA cable, disk, or controller.
finding.ata_errors.impact: Data corruption risk, slow I/O, system instability
finding.ata_errors.title: Frequent ATA/SATA Errors ({{count}} occurrences)
finding.backup_aging.action: Monitor the next scheduled run. Check logs for intermittent errors.
finding.backup_aging.description: Backup job '{{label}}' ({{kind}}) last succeeded {{ago}} ago (>24h). The job may be delayed or encountering intermittent issues.
finding.backup_aging.impact: Backup freshness degraded. Recovery may be missing recent changes.
finding.backup_aging.title: Backup aging: {{label}} ({{kind}}) — last success {{ago}} ago
finding.backup_failed.action: Investigate the backup error and re-run the job. Check repository access and disk space.
finding.backup_failed.impact: No recent backup available. Data loss risk if a failure occurs.
finding.backup_failed.title: Backup failed: {{label}} ({{kind}})
finding.backup_healthy.description: Backup job '{{label}}' ({{kind}}) is healthy with {{count}} snapshots totaling {{size}}.
finding.backup_healthy.title: Backup healthy: {{label}} ({{kind}}) — {{count}} snapshots, {{size}}
finding.backup_stale.action: Check if the backup schedule is running. Verify repository connectivity and credentials.
finding.backup_stale.description: Backup job '{{label}}' ({{kind}}) has not completed successfully in over 48 hours. Last success was {{ago}} ago.
finding.backup_stale.impact: Backup data is stale. Recovery point objective (RPO) exceeded.
finding.backup_stale.title: Backup stale: {{label}} ({{kind}}) — last success {{ago}} ago
finding.command_timeout.action: Check SATA cable and power connections. May indicate controller or drive issues.
finding.command_timeout.title: Command Timeouts on {{device}} ({{model}})
finding.container_cpu.action: Investigate the container workload immediately. Apply CPU limits (--cpus) or restart if stuck.
finding.container_cpu.description: Container '{{name}}' ({{image}}) is consuming {{cpu}}% CPU across multiple cores.
finding.container_cpu.impact: Severely starving other containers and host processes. May cause system instability.
finding.container_cpu.title: Extreme CPU: Container '{{name}}' ({{pct}}%)
finding.container_mem_exhausted.action: Set memory limits (--memory). Investigate memory leaks. Restart the container.
finding.container_mem_exhausted.descript: Container '{{name}}' ({{image}}) is using {{mem_pct}}% of available memory ({{mem}} MB).
finding.container_mem_exhausted.impact: Imminent OOM kill risk. Container or host may become unresponsive.
finding.container_mem_exhausted.title: Memory Exhaustion: Container '{{name}}' ({{pct}}%)
finding.container_mem_high.action: Monitor memory trends. Set memory limits or investigate the workload.
finding.container_mem_high.description: Container '{{name}}' ({{image}}) is using {{mem_pct}}% of available memory ({{mem}} MB).
finding.container_mem_high.impact: May trigger OOM killer if usage continues to grow.
finding.container_mem_high.title: High Memory: Container '{{name}}' ({{pct}}%)
finding.critical_disk_io.action: Add an SSD cache drive. Check for failing disks or bad SATA cables causing retries.
finding.critical_disk_io.description: I/O wait is at {{pct}}%. CPUs are spending a large portion of time waiting for disk operations.
finding.critical_disk_io.impact: Everything on the system feels slow — file transfers, Docker containers, application responsiveness
finding.critical_disk_io.title: Severe Disk I/O Bottleneck
finding.critical_memory.action: Identify memory-hungry processes. Consider adding RAM or reducing Docker container count.
finding.critical_memory.description: Memory usage is at {{pct}}% ({{used}} MB / {{total}} MB). The system may be swapping heavily or at risk of OOM kills.
finding.critical_memory.title: Critical Memory Pressure
finding.disk_nearly_full.action: Free space immediately or expand storage.
finding.disk_nearly_full.description: {{mount}} is at {{pct}}% capacity ({{free}} GB free of {{total}} GB).
finding.disk_nearly_full.impact: Services may fail if disk fills completely. Write operations will fail.
finding.disk_nearly_full.title: Disk Almost Full: {{mount}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.disk_space_low.action: Monitor growth rate. Plan storage expansion or cleanup.
finding.disk_space_low.description: {{mount}} is at {{pct}}% capacity ({{free}} GB free of {{total}} GB).
finding.disk_space_low.impact: May run out of space soon if growth continues
finding.disk_space_low.title: Low Disk Space: {{mount}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.drive_aging.action: Ensure backups are current. Consider proactive replacement.
finding.drive_aging.description: Drive {{device}} has {{hours}} power-on hours ({{years}} years). {{tier}}. Backblaze data shows failure rate at {{mult}}x baseline for drives at this age.
finding.drive_aging.impact: Increased probability of failure over time
finding.drive_aging.title: Aging Drive: {{device}} ({{model}})
finding.gpu_high_temp.action: Monitor trends. Improve airflow if temperature continues rising.
finding.gpu_high_temp.description: GPU '{{name}}' is running warm at {{temp}}°C. Most GPUs throttle between 83-95°C.
finding.gpu_high_temp.impact: May begin thermal throttling under sustained load.
finding.gpu_high_temp.title: GPU Temperature High: {{name}} at {{temp}}°C
finding.gpu_overheating.action: Improve case airflow. Clean heatsink/fans. Check thermal paste. Reduce workload.
finding.gpu_overheating.description: GPU '{{name}}' temperature is critically high at {{temp}}°C. Thermal throttling is active and sustained operation at this temperature reduces GPU lifespan.
finding.gpu_overheating.impact: Performance degradation from thermal throttling. Risk of hardware damage.
finding.gpu_overheating.title: GPU Overheating: {{name}} at {{temp}}°C
finding.gpu_power_limit.action: Check GPU BIOS settings and PSU capacity.
finding.gpu_power_limit.description: GPU '{{name}}' is drawing {{watts}}W against a {{limit}}W power limit. This may indicate a misconfigured power limit or faulty power delivery.
finding.gpu_power_limit.title: GPU Power Draw Exceeds Limit: {{name}}
finding.gpu_vram_full.action: Reduce concurrent GPU workloads or upgrade to a GPU with more VRAM.
finding.gpu_vram_full.description: GPU '{{name}}' VRAM utilization is at {{pct}}% ({{used}}/{{total}} MB). Applications may crash or fall back to system RAM.
finding.gpu_vram_full.impact: Transcoding failures, OOM kills for GPU workloads, degraded performance.
finding.gpu_vram_full.title: GPU VRAM Nearly Full: {{name}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.heavy_swap.action: Add more RAM. Review which processes are consuming the most memory.
finding.heavy_swap.description: Swap is {{used}}/{{total}} MB ({{pct}}% used). Active swapping causes severe I/O performance degradation.
finding.heavy_swap.impact: Significantly increased I/O load, overall system slowness
finding.heavy_swap.title: Heavy Swap Usage
finding.high_disk_io_wait.action: Consider adding an SSD cache for Docker containers and frequently-accessed data.
finding.high_disk_io_wait.description: I/O wait is at {{pct}}%. This is above the ideal threshold of <10%.
finding.high_disk_io_wait.impact: Noticeable performance degradation during heavy disk activity
finding.high_disk_io_wait.title: Elevated Disk I/O Wait
finding.high_load.action: Identify CPU-heavy processes. Reduce concurrent workloads or upgrade CPU.
finding.high_load.description: 5-minute load average ({{load}}) is more than 2x the CPU core count ({{cores}}). The system is overloaded.
finding.high_load.title: High System Load
finding.high_memory.action: Review container memory limits. Consider RAM upgrade if usage keeps growing.
finding.high_memory.description: Memory usage is at {{pct}}% ({{used}} MB / {{total}} MB).
finding.high_memory.impact: May cause slowdowns under additional load
finding.high_memory.title: High Memory Usage
finding.high_temp.action: Improve case airflow. Add/replace fans. Check that existing fans are working.
finding.high_temp.description: Drive {{device}} ({{model}}) is at {{temp}}°C. {{tier}} — Backblaze + Google research shows failure rate at {{mult}}x baseline at this temperature.
finding.high_temp.impact: Reduced drive lifespan, increased error rate
finding.high_temp.title: Drive Temperature: {{device}} at {{temp}}°C
finding.hist_overheat.action: Monitor SMART attributes closely for degradation.
finding.hist_overheat.description: Drive {{device}} has reached {{temp}}°C at some point in its lifetime. At this temperature, failure rate is ~{{mult}}x baseline. Thermal damage may be permanent.
finding.hist_overheat.impact: Possible latent damage from thermal stress
finding.hist_overheat.title: Historical Overheating on {{device}} (max {{temp}}°C)
finding.io_errors.action: Identify the affected drive from the error messages. Check SMART health.
finding.io_errors.description: Kernel logs show I/O errors. This means the system is unable to read or write to a disk.
finding.io_errors.title: I/O Errors Detected ({{count}} occurrences)
finding.k8s_container_failed.title: K8s pod failed: {{namespace}}/{{pod}}
finding.k8s_container_oom.action: Increase memory limits or optimize application memory usage
finding.k8s_container_oom.description: Pod {{pod}} was killed due to out-of-memory. Restarts: {{restarts}}
finding.k8s_container_oom.title: K8s pod OOM killed: {{namespace}}/{{pod}}
finding.k8s_container_oom_killed.descrip: Container {{container}} in pod {{pod}} was OOM killed (restarts: {{restarts}})
finding.k8s_container_oom_killed.impact: Container exceeded memory limit and was terminated
finding.k8s_container_oom_killed.title: K8s container OOM: {{namespace}}/{{pod}}/{{container}}
finding.k8s_container_pending.descriptio: Pod {{pod}} in namespace {{namespace}} is pending and not assigned to any node
finding.k8s_container_pending.impact: Workload is not running — may be waiting for resources
finding.k8s_container_pending.title: K8s pod pending (unscheduled): {{namespace}}/{{pod}}
finding.k8s_crashloop.description: Pod {{pod}} in namespace {{namespace}} is in CrashLoopBackOff with {{restarts}} restarts
finding.k8s_crashloop.impact: Application is repeatedly crashing and restarting
finding.k8s_crashloop.title: K8s pod crash loop: {{namespace}}/{{pod}}
finding.k8s_deployment_stopped.title: K8s deployment down: {{namespace}}/{{name}}
finding.k8s_deployment_unhealthy.action: Check pod status: kubectl get pods -l app={{name}} -n {{namespace}}
finding.k8s_deployment_unhealthy.title: K8s deployment unhealthy: {{namespace}}/{{name}}
finding.k8s_high_restarts.description: Pod {{pod}} has restarted {{count}} times. May indicate instability.
finding.k8s_high_restarts.title: K8s pod high restarts: {{namespace}}/{{pod}} ({{count}})
finding.k8s_image_pull_failed.action: Check image name, registry credentials, and network connectivity
finding.k8s_image_pull_failed.title: K8s image pull failed: {{namespace}}/{{pod}}
finding.k8s_node_evicted.description: Node {{node}} is marked unschedulable (cordoned). No new pods will be placed here.
finding.k8s_node_evicted.title: K8s node cordoned: {{node}}
finding.k8s_node_high_pods.action: Consider adding nodes or migrating workloads
finding.k8s_node_high_pods.impact: New pods may fail to schedule on this node
finding.k8s_node_high_pods.title: K8s node pod capacity high: {{node}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.k8s_node_not_ready.action: Check node health: kubectl describe node {{node}}
finding.k8s_node_not_ready.description: Node {{node}} is in '{{status}}' state. Roles: {{roles}}, Version: {{version}}
finding.k8s_node_not_ready.impact: Pods on this node may be evicted or unable to schedule
finding.k8s_node_not_ready.title: K8s node not ready: {{node}}
finding.k8s_node_pressure.impact: Pods may be evicted to relieve pressure
finding.k8s_node_pressure.title: K8s node pressure: {{condition}} on {{node}}
finding.k8s_pvc_lost.action: Investigate PV status and storage backend immediately
finding.k8s_pvc_lost.description: PersistentVolumeClaim {{name}} has lost its backing volume
finding.k8s_pvc_lost.title: K8s PVC lost: {{namespace}}/{{name}}
finding.k8s_pvc_pending.action: Check storage provisioner and available PVs
finding.k8s_pvc_pending.impact: Pods depending on this PVC cannot start
finding.k8s_pvc_pending.title: K8s PVC pending: {{namespace}}/{{name}}
finding.low_health_score.action: Plan replacement. Ensure backups are current and verified.
finding.low_health_score.description: Drive {{device}} ({{model}}) has a composite health score of {{score}}/100 based on Backblaze failure rate data. Multiple risk factors are combining to create elevated failure probability.
finding.low_health_score.title: Low Health Score: {{device}} at {{score}}/100
finding.network_down.action: Check cable connection and switch port.
finding.network_down.title: Network Interface Down: {{iface}}
finding.no_ssd_cache.action: Add an SSD or NVMe cache drive. Move Docker appdata to the cache.
finding.no_ssd_cache.description: Running {{count}} Docker containers without an SSD cache drive. All container I/O goes to the array's spinning disks, creating I/O contention.
finding.no_ssd_cache.impact: Docker containers compete with array operations for disk I/O, causing overall slowness.
finding.no_ssd_cache.title: No SSD Cache with Docker Workloads
finding.parity_errors.action: Run a correcting parity check. Investigate which drive has bad data.
finding.parity_errors.impact: Parity data is inconsistent. Array protection is compromised.
finding.parity_errors.title: Parity Errors on {{date}}
finding.parity_speed_critical.action: Check SATA cables, drive health, and controller. The slowest drive/cable is the bottleneck.
finding.parity_speed_critical.descriptio: Parity check speed has degraded by {{pct}}% (from {{old}} MB/s to {{new}} MB/s). This is a strong indicator of a hardware issue.
finding.parity_speed_critical.impact: Parity checks take much longer, array is unprotected for extended periods
finding.parity_speed_critical.title: Severe Parity Check Speed Degradation
finding.parity_speed_decline.action: Monitor trend. Check SATA cables if degradation continues.
finding.parity_speed_decline.description: Parity check speed has dropped {{pct}}% (from {{old}} MB/s to {{new}} MB/s).
finding.parity_speed_decline.impact: Longer parity checks, reduced array performance
finding.parity_speed_decline.title: Parity Check Speed Declining
finding.parity_temp.action: Address cooling before evaluating parity performance further.
finding.parity_temp.description: Multiple drives are running hot, which can cause thermal throttling and reduced I/O performance.
finding.parity_temp.impact: Drives may throttle to protect themselves, slowing array operations.
finding.parity_temp.title: Correlation: High Temperatures May Be Affecting Parity Speed
finding.pending_sectors.action: Run an extended SMART self-test. Plan drive replacement.
finding.pending_sectors.description: Drive {{device}} has {{count}} pending sectors. {{tier}} — Backblaze data shows drives with pending sectors fail at {{mult}}x the baseline rate.
finding.pending_sectors.impact: Active read errors, data corruption risk
finding.pending_sectors.title: Pending Sectors on {{device}} ({{model}})
finding.pve_backup_stale.action: Check Datacenter → Backup in PVE to verify backup jobs are scheduled and running
finding.pve_backup_stale.description: Last successful backup was {{hours}} hours ago. Consider verifying your backup schedule.
finding.pve_backup_stale.impact: Data loss risk if a VM fails without recent backup
finding.pve_backup_stale.title: Proxmox backups may be stale
finding.pve_guest_mem_critical.action: Increase memory allocation or optimize applications
finding.pve_guest_mem_critical.descripti: VMID {{vmid}} ({{name}}) is using {{pct}}% of {{total}} GB allocated memory
finding.pve_guest_mem_critical.impact: Application performance issues or crashes inside the guest
finding.pve_guest_mem_critical.title: Guest memory critical: {{name}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.pve_ha_error.action: Check HA logs, verify fencing configuration, check node health
finding.pve_ha_error.description: HA service {{sid}} on node {{node}} is in state '{{state}}': {{status}}
finding.pve_ha_error.title: PVE HA service error: {{sid}}
finding.pve_ha_guest_stopped.action: Check PVE HA logs, verify guest can start, check for resource constraints
finding.pve_ha_guest_stopped.description: {{type}} {{name}} on node {{node}} is stopped but configured for HA with state 'started'. This indicates an HA failure.
finding.pve_ha_guest_stopped.impact: Service outage for applications running in this guest
finding.pve_ha_guest_stopped.title: HA-managed guest stopped: {{name}} (VMID {{vmid}})
finding.pve_node_cpu_high.action: Identify high-CPU VMs, consider migrating workloads
finding.pve_node_cpu_high.title: Proxmox node CPU high: {{node}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.pve_node_mem_critical.action: Migrate VMs to other nodes, increase RAM, or reduce VM memory allocations
finding.pve_node_mem_critical.descriptio: Node {{node}} is using {{pct}}% of {{total}} GB RAM. VMs may be killed by the OOM killer.
finding.pve_node_mem_critical.impact: Risk of VM/container termination due to out-of-memory
finding.pve_node_mem_critical.title: Proxmox node memory critical: {{node}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.pve_node_mem_high.action: Consider migrating workloads or adding more RAM
finding.pve_node_mem_high.description: Node {{node}} is using {{pct}}% of {{total}} GB RAM.
finding.pve_node_mem_high.impact: Performance degradation, risk of OOM if usage increases
finding.pve_node_mem_high.title: Proxmox node memory high: {{node}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.pve_node_offline.action: Check physical server power, network connectivity, and PVE cluster logs
finding.pve_node_offline.description: Node {{node}} is reporting status '{{status}}'. This may indicate a hardware failure, network issue, or planned maintenance.
finding.pve_node_offline.impact: VMs and containers on this node are unavailable
finding.pve_node_offline.title: Proxmox node offline: {{node}}
finding.pve_storage_critical.action: Free space immediately: remove old backups, snapshots, or unused disk images
finding.pve_storage_critical.description: Storage pool '{{storage}}' ({{type}}) on node {{node}} is {{pct}}% full. Total: {{total}} GB
finding.pve_storage_critical.impact: Cannot create snapshots, backups, or new VMs. Running VMs may fail on disk writes.
finding.pve_storage_critical.title: PVE storage critical: {{storage}} on {{node}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.pve_storage_high.description: Storage pool '{{storage}}' ({{type}}) on node {{node}} is {{pct}}% full
finding.pve_storage_high.impact: May run out of space for backups and snapshots
finding.pve_storage_high.title: PVE storage high: {{storage}} on {{node}} ({{pct}}%)
finding.pve_task_failed.action: Check task log in PVE for details
finding.pve_task_failed.description: Task {{task}} for VMID {{vmid}} on node {{node}} finished with status: {{status}}
finding.pve_task_failed.title: PVE task failed: {{task}} on {{node}}
finding.reallocated_sectors.action: Monitor closely. Plan replacement if count is increasing.
finding.reallocated_sectors.description: Drive {{device}} has {{count}} reallocated sectors. {{tier}} — Backblaze data ({{version}}) shows drives at this level fail at {{mult}}x the baseline rate.
finding.reallocated_sectors.impact: Progressive drive failure, potential data loss
finding.reallocated_sectors.title: Reallocated Sectors on {{device}} ({{model}})
finding.root_cause_sata.action: Replace the affected SATA cable(s). This is the #1 priority fix.
finding.root_cause_sata.description: UDMA CRC errors are directly correlated with parity check speed degradation. A failing SATA cable forces the controller to retry operations, dramatically slowing array-wide operations.
finding.root_cause_sata.impact: Until the cable is replaced, parity checks and array performance will continue to degrade.
finding.root_cause_sata.title: Root Cause: SATA Cable Failure Causing Parity Degradation
finding.sata_cable.action: Replace the SATA cable on port {{port}}. Use a certified SATA III cable.
finding.sata_cable.description: Drive {{device}} has {{count}} UDMA CRC errors. {{tier}}. CRC errors indicate data transfer corruption — almost always a cable/connection issue, not the drive itself.
finding.sata_cable.impact: Slow I/O, transfer errors, parity check slowdowns
finding.sata_cable.title: SATA Cable Issue on {{device}} ({{model}})
finding.service_check_failed.action: Verify the service process, endpoint reachability, network path, and authentication/configuration for this target.
finding.service_check_failed.description: {{type}} check for {{target}} is failing ({{count}} consecutive failures).
finding.service_check_failed.impact: Dependent applications and clients may fail while this service remains unavailable.
finding.service_check_failed.title: Service Check Failed: {{name}}
finding.slow_link.action: Replace Ethernet cable. Check switch port.
finding.slow_link.description: Interface {{iface}} is negotiated at 100Mb/s instead of 1Gb/s or higher. This is usually caused by a bad cable or switch port.
finding.slow_link.impact: Network transfers capped at ~12 MB/s instead of ~120 MB/s
finding.slow_link.title: Slow Link Speed: {{iface}} at 100Mb/s
finding.smart_health_failed.action: Replace this drive immediately. Back up any unique data NOW.
finding.smart_health_failed.description: Drive {{device}} (S/N: {{serial}}) has FAILED its SMART self-assessment. This drive is at imminent risk of failure.
finding.smart_health_failed.impact: Data loss if the drive fails before data is migrated
finding.smart_health_failed.title: SMART Health FAILED: {{device}} ({{model}})
finding.smart_unavailable.action: Check if the drive supports SMART passthrough. For USB drives, try enabling SAT passthrough. For HBA controllers, verify smartctl can access the drive directly.
finding.smart_unavailable.description: Drive {{device}} ({{model}}) was detected but smartctl could not read SMART attributes. The drive may be behind an HBA, USB bridge, or unsupported controller.
finding.smart_unavailable.impact: Drive health cannot be monitored — failures may go undetected
finding.smart_unavailable.title: SMART data unavailable: {{device}}
finding.stopped_containers.action: Review stopped containers. Remove ones that aren't needed: docker container prune
finding.stopped_containers.description: {{count}} containers are in exited/dead state. These may be failed or unused.
finding.stopped_containers.impact: Wasted disk space, potential confusion in management
finding.stopped_containers.title: {{count}} Stopped Containers
finding.synology_unmounted.action: Stop the container, add `/volume1:/host/volume1:ro` (and one line per additional volume) to your docker-compose.yml or Container Manager configuration, then restart. See the Synology DSM section of the README for the full mount list.
finding.synology_unmounted.description: The container is running on a Synology DSM host but has no /volume* paths visible. Storage tracking is incomplete — the dashboard is showing DSM system partitions, not your actual user storage.
finding.synology_unmounted.impact: User volumes (/volume1, /volume2, ...) are invisible to NAS Doctor. Free-space alerts, disk-space findings, and capacity tracking will not fire for the storage you actually care about.
finding.synology_unmounted.title: Synology storage volumes not bind-mounted
finding.system_outdated.action: Plan an update soon. Back up your configuration first.
finding.system_outdated.description: You are {{major}} major/{{minor}} minor versions behind. Significantly outdated OS versions may have unpatched security vulnerabilities.
finding.system_outdated.title: NAS OS Significantly Out of Date ({{current}} → {{new}})
finding.systematic_thermal.action: Check all case fans are operational. Consider adding intake/exhaust fans. Clean dust filters.
finding.systematic_thermal.description: {{count}} drives are running hot ({{drives}}). This suggests a case-level airflow problem rather than individual drive issues.
finding.systematic_thermal.impact: Accelerated wear across the entire array
finding.systematic_thermal.title: Systemic Thermal Issue
finding.updates_available.action: Update your NAS OS when convenient. Review release notes before updating.
finding.updates_available.description: You are running {{os}} {{current}}. Version {{new}} is available. Keeping your NAS OS up to date ensures you have the latest security patches and bug fixes.
finding.updates_available.impact: Missing security patches and bug fixes.
finding.updates_available.title: OS Update Available: {{os}} {{current}} → {{new}}
finding.ups_battery_low.description: UPS battery is critically low at {{pct}}% with approximately {{minutes}} minutes remaining.
finding.ups_battery_low.impact: Imminent unclean shutdown. Data corruption risk.
finding.ups_battery_low.title: UPS Low Battery ({{pct}}%)
finding.ups_load_critical.description: UPS '{{name}}' is at {{pct}}% load ({{watts}}W / {{max}}W). May fail to protect equipment.
finding.ups_load_critical.impact: UPS may fail to provide backup power.
finding.ups_load_critical.title: UPS Overloaded ({{pct}}% load)
finding.ups_load_high.action: Consider upgrading UPS or reducing load.
finding.ups_load_high.description: UPS '{{name}}' is at {{pct}}% load. Keep below 75% for adequate headroom.
finding.ups_load_high.title: UPS High Load ({{pct}}%)
finding.ups_not_charged.action: Replace battery if it stays below 80% after several hours of charging.
finding.ups_not_charged.description: UPS battery is at {{pct}}% while on mains power. This may indicate a degraded battery.
finding.ups_not_charged.impact: Reduced backup time during power outage.
finding.ups_not_charged.title: UPS Battery Not Fully Charged ({{pct}}%)
finding.ups_on_battery.action: Check mains power. If outage is extended, initiate graceful shutdown.
finding.ups_on_battery.description: UPS '{{name}}' ({{model}}) is running on battery power.
finding.ups_on_battery.impact: Server will shut down when battery is depleted.
finding.ups_on_battery.title: UPS On Battery — {{name}}
finding.ups_replace_battery.description: UPS '{{name}}' is reporting that its battery needs replacement.
finding.ups_replace_battery.impact: UPS may not provide adequate backup time.
finding.ups_replace_battery.title: UPS Battery Replacement Needed
finding.ups_runtime_short.description: Only {{minutes}} minutes of estimated runtime at current load. Not enough for graceful shutdown.

finding.zfs_arc_low.action: Add more RAM to increase ARC size, or add an L2ARC (SSD cache).
finding.zfs_arc_low.description: The ZFS ARC (Adaptive Replacement Cache) has a hit rate of {{pct}}%. Ideally this should be above 90%. Low hit rates mean more disk reads.
finding.zfs_arc_low.impact: Increased disk I/O, slower file access.
finding.zfs_arc_low.title: Low ZFS ARC Hit Rate ({{pct}}%)
finding.zfs_data_errors.action: Run 'zpool scrub' to repair. Restore affected files from backup if needed.
finding.zfs_data_errors.impact: Data corruption detected. Affected files may be unreadable.
finding.zfs_data_errors.title: Data Errors on Pool '{{pool}}'
finding.zfs_degraded.action: Replace the failed device immediately with 'zpool replace'. {{hint}}
finding.zfs_degraded.description: Pool '{{pool}}' is operating in degraded mode — one or more devices has failed or been removed. The pool has reduced redundancy and cannot survive another device failure.
finding.zfs_degraded.impact: No redundancy. Another device failure will cause data loss.
finding.zfs_degraded.title: ZFS Pool '{{pool}}' is DEGRADED
finding.zfs_device_errors.action: Check SMART health of the underlying drive. Replace if errors are increasing.
finding.zfs_device_errors.description: Device {{device}} in pool '{{pool}}' has {{count}} total errors. Checksum errors indicate data corruption. Read/write errors indicate hardware issues.
finding.zfs_device_errors.impact: Data integrity risk. Drive may be failing.
finding.zfs_device_errors.title: ZFS Device Errors: {{device}} in '{{pool}}'
finding.zfs_faulted.action: Investigate failed devices. Restore from backup if necessary.
finding.zfs_faulted.description: Pool '{{pool}}' is in a FAULTED state and cannot be accessed. Too many devices have failed for the pool to continue operating.
finding.zfs_faulted.impact: Pool is offline. Data is inaccessible until repaired.
finding.zfs_faulted.title: ZFS Pool '{{pool}}' is FAULTED
finding.zfs_fragmentation.action: Fragmentation is often caused by high pool usage. Free space to reduce fragmentation.
finding.zfs_fragmentation.description: Pool '{{pool}}' has {{pct}}% fragmentation. High fragmentation reduces write performance, especially for large sequential writes.
finding.zfs_fragmentation.title: High Fragmentation on Pool '{{pool}}' ({{pct}}%)
finding.zfs_high_capacity.action: Free space or expand the pool. ZFS recommends keeping usage below 80%.
finding.zfs_high_capacity.description: Pool '{{pool}}' is {{pct}}% full ({{used}} GB used of {{total}} GB). ZFS performance degrades significantly above 80% capacity due to fragmentation.
finding.zfs_high_capacity.impact: Write performance degradation, potential inability to write.
finding.zfs_high_capacity.title: ZFS Pool '{{pool}}' at {{pct}}% Capacity
finding.zfs_no_scrub.action: Schedule weekly or monthly scrubs: 'zpool scrub {{pool}}'
finding.zfs_no_scrub.description: Pool '{{pool}}' has never been scrubbed. Regular scrubs detect silent data corruption (bit rot) before it becomes unrecoverable.
finding.zfs_no_scrub.impact: Silent data corruption may go undetected.
finding.zfs_no_scrub.title: No Scrub History for Pool '{{pool}}'
finding.zfs_resilver.action: Wait for resilver to complete. Do not remove any other drives.
finding.zfs_resilver.description: Pool '{{pool}}' is currently resilvering (rebuilding) a replaced device. The pool has reduced redundancy until complete.
finding.zfs_resilver.impact: Pool is vulnerable during resilver. Avoid heavy I/O.
finding.zfs_resilver.title: Resilver in Progress on '{{pool}}' ({{pct}}%)
finding.zfs_scrub_errors.action: Run 'zpool scrub {{pool}}' to repair. Check drive health with SMART.
finding.zfs_scrub_errors.description: The last scrub of pool '{{pool}}' found {{count}} errors. This means data corruption has been detected.
finding.zfs_scrub_errors.impact: Data integrity compromised. Affected files may be corrupted.
finding.zfs_scrub_errors.title: ZFS Scrub Errors on '{{pool}}' ({{count}} errors)
finding.zfs_unavailable.action: Check physical connections. Import with 'zpool import -f' if needed.
finding.zfs_unavailable.description: Pool '{{pool}}' cannot be opened. The required devices are missing or corrupted.
finding.zfs_unavailable.title: ZFS Pool '{{pool}}' is UNAVAILABLE

settings.advanced.borg.desc: Monitor externally-managed BorgBackup repos (e.g. Unraid User Scripts setups) by bind-mounting the repo path into the NAS Doctor container. The borg binary is bundled in the image; you only need to mount the repo. Set BORG_PASSPHRASE in Docker env vars for encrypted repos.
settings.advanced.borg.title: Backup Monitors → Borg
settings.advanced.desc: Expert-only knobs for SMART scan controls (wake Drives, max-age safety net), Docker container visibility, and more. Defaults are safe — only change these if you understand the trade-offs.
settings.advanced.docker_hide.desc: Tick the containers you want hidden from the Docker Containers section. Stats history is still collected and alerts still fire — the containers are hidden from the tile, not suppressed. Top Processes container attribution is not affected: if a hidden container is chewing CPU you'll still see its name there.
settings.advanced.docker_hide.title: Hide Docker containers from dashboard
settings.advanced.duplicacy.desc: Monitor Duplicacy backups by bind-mounting either the repo root (CLI install) or the cache directory (saspus/duplicacy-web) into NAS Doctor. Disk-read only — the duplicacy binary is never invoked. Pick CLI repo for vanilla installs (path is the repo root); pick Web cache for duplicacy-web (path is the cache root, plus the per-repo storage id).
settings.advanced.duplicacy.title: Backup Monitors → Duplicacy
settings.advanced.intervals.desc: Override the global scan cadence per subsystem. Use Use global to inherit the Diagnostic Scan Interval (most users want this). Set a positive interval only if you want that subsystem to run faster or slower than the rest of the dashboard. Values persist immediately, but no scheduler behaviour changes until the slice-2b release.
settings.advanced.intervals.title: Per-subsystem scan intervals
settings.advanced.smart.max_age.desc: If a drive stays in standby longer than this many days without a successful SMART read, NAS Doctor will force one wake-up to refresh SMART data. Lower values keep SMART data fresher at the cost of more spin-ups; higher values reduce wear but let drives go longer unobserved. Set to 0 to disable the safety net entirely — SMART will never force a wake-up (v0.9.5 behaviour). Valid range 0–30.
settings.advanced.smart.max_age.label: Max days without SMART read
settings.advanced.smart.title: SMART scan controls
settings.advanced.smart.wake_desc: By default, NAS Doctor skips drives that are in standby — SMART history will show gaps when drives are sleeping, and that's intentional (reduces wear). Enabling this option forces smartctl to wake spun-down drives on every scan cycle. At the default 30-min scan interval, that's roughly 48 extra spin-ups per drive per day. Only enable if your drives never spin down, or if you deliberately need every-cycle SMART monitoring and accept the wear cost.
settings.advanced.title: Advanced
